title: Proposal draft: Diabetes prevention service line (proposal)

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: About one in three primary care adults at the client has prediabetes on paper, and almost nobody is in a program. The client has a diabetes education class at one hospital and a lifestyle pilot in three clinics that lost its funding. The two largest employers are asking what the client offers before their renewals in July. The client does not want another pilot that disappears when a grant ends.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.body:
1. Show where adults with prediabetes are today across the 24 clinics, and what happens after a high A1c result.
2. Design a care model with a primary care front door, including how the lifestyle program and medication fit together.
3. Build an employer offer the two largest employers could contract for, with pricing the CFO can review.
4. Give the board a launch plan it can consider in April.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.body:
Phase 1: Discover (about weeks 1 to 4)
- Map prediabetes prevalence, A1c follow-up and leakage across the clinics
- Open employer and CFO conversations alongside the diagnostic
- Diagnostic readout at SteerCo 1
Phase 2: Diagnose and Design (about weeks 5 to 10)
- Interviews with patients, clinicians and employers; co-design workshops
- Front door and lifestyle plus medication care model options, with the clinical lead
- Options at SteerCo 2
Phase 3: Deliver (to the April board)
- Employer offer and pricing, governance, launch plan
- Final recommendation as a board pre-read

sections.heading: Workstreams
sections.body:
1. Prediabetes diagnostic: population, A1c follow-up and what happens after a high result.
2. Care model and primary care front door, including lifestyle program and medication.
3. Employer offer and pricing for the two largest employers.
4. Launch plan and governance for the April board.

sections.heading: Deliverables
sections.body: Diagnostic readout (SteerCo 1). Care model options with front door design (SteerCo 2). Employer offer and pricing model for CFO review. Governance design. Launch plan and final recommendation as the April board pre-read.

sources.quote: A launch plan for the April board.

sections.heading: Timeline
sections.body: Start in the first week of January, with a final recommendation ready for the April board. Three SteerCos, after the diagnostic, after care model options and at the final readout, as on past engagements. Total weeks and SteerCo dates to be fixed once the April board date is known.

sources.quote: start in first week of January; something ready for the April board

sections.heading: Assumptions and exclusions
sections.body:
Out of scope, as on past engagements: IT system build, clinical protocol authorship, recruitment.
The CMO owns the clinical model, so we assume a named clinical lead who sits in governance from the start; early clinical voice in governance unlocked design on a past engagement.
The CFO signs off employer pricing, so we assume CFO time early; a past employer bundle needed it two weeks sooner than planned.
Employer conversations start alongside the diagnostic; on a past engagement a late-scoped payer contract forced an extension.
The offer should be designed to be funded on an ongoing basis, not as a grant-funded pilot.

questions.text: How many patient, clinician and employer interviews?
questions.fallback: 20 to 25, as on a past weight management engagement; a behavioral health engagement used 12.

questions.text: Is employer pricing in scope as a built model, or advice only?
questions.fallback: In scope as a model the CFO can review, as on a past employer bundle, with CFO time booked two weeks earlier than before.
Alongside the diagnostic in weeks 1 to 4, because a past payer contract scoped in week 10 led to a four-week extension.

questions.text: How many weeks in total, given the April board date?
questions.fallback: 16 weeks, as on a past weight management engagement, trimmed to fit the board date.

questions.text: How much on-site time for the partner and the team?
questions.fallback: Partner half a day a week, manager or lead and consultant full time, as on past engagements.

questions.text: Does the named clinical lead from the CMO's office sit on the steering group from kickoff?
questions.fallback: Yes, from week 1, because getting surgery a vote in governance early unlocked the design on a past engagement.
